turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Work stuff. I got let go a few weeks ago. It's okay, I needed the break anyway. I've had some trouble sleeping, but that's about it.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That must have been difficult. Is there anything else going on that you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My neighbors. They can be a bit...loud at times. Sometimes I swear I hear them talking about me, but when I try to listen closer, it's just my stereo or the TV.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That must be unnerving. Do you want to talk more about that?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (slightly deflecting) Oh, it's just part of living in an apartment building, I guess. It's not a big deal. I've just gotten used to it. (pausing, then changing the subject) How did you get here today, by the way?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I took the bus. I like taking the bus because it gives me time to think and relax.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (skeptical) Yeah, buses can be okay, I guess. I've never really been a fan of them, though. Too much noise and people. (muttering to self) Like, I don't even know why they always have to have music blaring on there...

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (smiling) I know what you mean. Music can be a bit much at times. How about we talk a bit more about how you're feeling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (tightening up) I'm feeling fine. Just a bit...tired, I suppose. It's been a lot of changes lately, and it's hard to keep up. (looking away, avoiding eye contact) That's all.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (in a gentle tone) Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (hesitating, then slowly) Sometimes I feel like I'm being watched, even when I'm alone in my apartment. I know it sounds silly, but... (trailing off, not elaborating)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (listening carefully) Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking down, fidgeting) No, that's all. I think. (pausing, then glancing up) You're not going to try to tell me what's going on with my neighbors, or anything, are you?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (nodding) Of course not. I'm here to listen and support you however I can. Is there anything else we should talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (eyes narrowing slightly) I don't know...I just don't want to get into this whole thing, you know? It's just... (pausing, then looking away) sometimes it feels like I'm the only one who knows what's going on, and it's hard to deal with.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (understanding) It can be difficult to feel like you're the only one who knows something. Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (frowning slightly) No...I don't think so. I'm just tired, that's all. This conversation is... (pausing, then looking at you warily) exhausting.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (smiling) I understand. Is there anything else we should talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shaking head) No, I think we're done. Thank you, I guess. (standing up, indicating the session is over)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: You're welcome. Is there anything else I can do to help?
